title: Learned prognostic screening links miR-130b-3p and NR3C2 to a putative kidney-cancer relationship
summary: An integrative analysis of clear-cell renal cell carcinoma used learned prognostic models and co-expression/target-gene intersections to prioritize NR3C2 and examine its relationship with miR-130b-3p. In 786-O cells, inhibiting miR-130b-3p increased NR3C2 mRNA and reduced proliferation, migration and invasion. The authors present the combined relationship as an extension of earlier work on each marker. Direct binding and NR3C2-dependent mediation were not established; the assays used one cell line. Prognostic evaluation was retrospective and subject to model-selection and feature-screening optimism, and it does not establish clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Integrative learned survival models; StepCox forward selection and LASSO-Cox modeling
organization: Southern Medical University; Hong Kong Baptist University; General Hospital of Southern Theater Command

evidence.tested: TCGA-KIRC model development used 516 patients/171 deaths and 99 candidate model combinations; the selected model retained 41 genes. Integrating its genes with co-expression modules and predicted targets identified NR3C2. Cell experiments in 786-O cells linked miR-130b-3p inhibition to increased NR3C2 mRNA and reduced proliferation, migration and invasion.
evidence.unknown: Direct miRNA binding and NR3C2 mediation remain untested. The authors identify prior work on both markers. GSE40914 performance helped select the model, so it is not fully independent validation; feature screening was not nested, and the model had about 4.2 events per retained variable. Generalization and therapeutic benefit are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Learned survival-model comparison and selection supplied a prognostic gene signature intersected with co-expression and predicted target-gene sets to prioritize NR3C2; LASSO-Cox modeling combined the two markers.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full-text sections 2.1–2.6, 3.5–3.7, Discussion and Conclusions; complete abstract, article date/affiliations and source-reported cell-assay results. Publisher-deposited Crossref metadata. No independent experiment or supplement review.
